title: upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops + rope/rotary + KV batching + scheduler tuning
author: Elena Martinez
description:
Motivation: Replace legacy attention kernels with FlashAttentionV2 and introduce fused rotary/ROPE ops, combined with a KV-batching-friendly path and scheduler heuristics to reduce tail latency and increase throughput. This PR addresses ENG-4123 (attention kernel upgrade), ENG-4180 (KV batching integration), and touches scheduling heuristics tracked in ENG-4245.

Summary of changes: upgraded third-party FlashAttention integration to V2 ABI-compatible kernels; implemented fused rotary/ROPE operators that are JIT-optimized for the V2 kernel codepath; added a fused-KV batching path that coalesces small KV cache updates to amortize kernel launch overhead; tuned scheduler heuristics to prefer fused ops for common sequence-length distributions and to avoid over-batching on strict latency SLO routes. Also includes benchmarks, unit tests, integration tests, and a staged canary rollout plan.

Checklist:
- [x] Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels and compatibility layer
- [x] Implement fused rope/rotary ops and add CPU fallback
- [x] Add KV-batching path and scheduler selection heuristics
- [x] Add microbenchmarks and end-to-end perf canary
- [x] Update docs and migration notes
- [x] Run full CI and perf regression suite

Compatibility and safety: The new kernel path is behind a feature flag and runtime capability check. The PR preserves legacy kernels as a fallback and exposes an environment variable (REDWOOD_USE_FLASHATTNV2) for controlled rollouts. No user-visible API changes.

Performance summary (canary on p3dn.24xlarge-like instance): median throughput +18% for autoregressive workloads (seq=1024, batch=8), p95 latency reduced by ~12% on average, end-to-end token compute cost down ~22% for long-context workloads due to fused ops and KV batching. Small-sequence, very low-latency routes see neutral to slight improvements; rolling policy keeps those on legacy path until validated.

Testing and rollout: unit tests added for fused rope ops and KV batching. Integration tests validate correctness against reference attention outputs (float32 and quantized paths). Perf canary ran across three accounts and showed stable improvements; rollout plan: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full over 2 weeks, with automatic rollback on quality regressions or latency p95 increases >5%.

Notes: The PR includes a small ABI shim for the FlashAttention vendor library; packaging notes are in contrib/third_party/flashattn/README.md. Follow-up work will cover additional quantized kernel paths and hardware-specific kernel selection tuning.

test: add unit/integration tests for new kernel paths
docs: performance notes and rollout plan
release_notes: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused ROPE/rotary ops, KV-batching optimizations, and scheduler heuristics. Performance improvements for long-context autoregressive workloads. Feature is behind flag and rolled out via canary.
discussion: Jared Lin: Can you confirm FP16 numerical parity across the fused path? - Answer: We run FP32 reference and FP16 fused path diff tests; differences are within expected rounding tolerances (max abs diff < 1e-3) for our test models.

Priya Natarajan: Scheduler heuristics look risky for low-latency routes. Suggest adding explicit opt-out based on route tags. - Reply: Added route-level opt-out and automatic fallback when p95 increases are detected.
Marco Rossi: CI failed once on integration timeout, reran and passed; please keep an eye on flaky bench infra. - Reply: Increased timeout and added retry on bench infra fetch.
Anika Singh (QA): Verified canary across 3 accounts; no correctness regressions observed for test prompt set.
benchmarks: token_cost: -22% for long-context workloads due to fused ops + KV batching
test_plan: Unit tests for fused ops and KV batcher, integration against reference attention outputs, perf canary across 3 accounts, staged rollout with automated rollback if p95 latency regresses >5% or quality alerts trigger.
notes: The FlashAttentionV2 vendor crate is included as an optional dependency. Packaging and license info in contrib/third_party/flashattn/README.md. Follow-up ticket created for quantized V2 kernels (ENG-4302).
